report.title: MRI BRAIN WITHOUT CONTRAST
report.indication: Headaches, more frequent over several weeks. Evaluate for intracranial abnormality.
report.technique: Multiplanar, multisequence MR imaging of the brain without intravenous contrast: sagittal T1, axial T1, T2, FLAIR and T2* gradient echo, coronal FLAIR, and diffusion-weighted imaging with ADC maps.
findings: Brain parenchyma: Normal gray-white matter differentiation. No mass, mass effect or midline shift. No focal signal abnormality on the FLAIR or T2-weighted images.
Diffusion: No restricted diffusion to suggest acute infarct.
Hemorrhage: No intracranial hemorrhage. No susceptibility artifact on the gradient echo images to suggest prior hemorrhage.
Ventricles and extra-axial spaces: Ventricles, sulci and basal cisterns are normal in size and configuration for age. No extra-axial fluid collection.
Posterior fossa: The cerebellum and brainstem are unremarkable. The cerebellar tonsils are in normal position.
Vessels: Normal flow voids in the major intracranial arteries and dural venous sinuses.
Other: The orbits are unremarkable. The visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear.
impression: Normal MRI of the brain without contrast. No intracranial abnormality to account for the headaches.

clinical.reason: Headaches, more frequent over several weeks.

code.display: CT Abdomen and Pelvis W contrast PO and W contrast IV

report.title: CT ABDOMEN AND PELVIS WITH ORAL AND IV CONTRAST
report.technique: Helical CT of the abdomen and pelvis after oral contrast and 85 mL of intravenous iodinated contrast (Isovue-300), with coronal and sagittal reformats. 120 kVp. CTDIvol 11.02 mGy; total DLP 562.59 mGy-cm.
findings: Lower chest: The lung bases are clear. Heart size is normal. No pleural or pericardial effusion.
Liver: Normal size and attenuation. No focal lesion. No biliary dilatation.
Gallbladder: Unremarkable.
Spleen, pancreas and adrenal glands: Unremarkable.
Kidneys: Symmetric enhancement. No hydronephrosis or renal calculus.

Bowel: Oral contrast opacifies normal-caliber small bowel. No bowel obstruction or wall thickening. Moderate stool in the colon. The appendix is not well seen; there is no pericecal inflammation or fluid collection.
Peritoneum and mesentery: No free air or free fluid. No lymphadenopathy.
Pelvis: The urinary bladder is unremarkable.
Vessels: The abdominal aorta is normal in caliber.
Bones and soft tissues: No acute or aggressive osseous abnormality.
impression: No acute abnormality in the abdomen or pelvis to explain the abdominal pain.

report.title: XR WRIST LEFT, 3 VIEWS
report.indication: Fall onto outstretched hands. Left wrist pain.
report.technique: PA, oblique and lateral views of the left wrist.
findings: Bones: No acute fracture. The distal radius and ulna are intact. The scaphoid is intact on these views.
Alignment: Normal radiocarpal and intercarpal alignment. No dislocation.
Joints: Joint spaces are preserved.
Soft tissues: No significant soft tissue swelling.
impression: No acute fracture or dislocation of the left wrist.

clinical.reason: Fall onto outstretched hands; left wrist pain.

code.display: XR Wrist - right and Hand - right GE 3 Views

report.title: XR HAND AND WRIST RIGHT, 3 VIEWS
report.indication: Fall onto outstretched hands. Pain over the fourth and fifth metacarpals.
report.technique: PA, oblique and lateral views of the right hand and wrist.
findings: Bones: No displaced fracture. The metacarpals and phalanges are intact on these views. The distal radius, ulna and carpal bones are intact.
Alignment: Normal. No dislocation.
Joints: Joint spaces are preserved.
Soft tissues: Mild soft tissue swelling over the ulnar side of the hand.
impression: No displaced fracture or dislocation of the right hand or wrist.
If pain persists over the fifth metacarpal, follow-up radiographs in 10 to 14 days can exclude an occult fracture.

clinical.reason: Fall onto outstretched hands; right hand pain over the fourth and fifth metacarpals.

report.title: XR HAND RIGHT, 3 VIEWS, PORTABLE
report.indication: Right hand injury, treated with an ulnar gutter splint for clinically suspected fifth metacarpal injury. Post-splint radiographs.
report.comparison: Right hand and wrist radiographs from 2012-10-10 01:37.
report.technique: Portable PA, oblique and lateral views of the right hand, taken through a splint.
findings: Splint: An ulnar gutter splint extends from the forearm over the fourth and fifth rays. The splint material obscures fine bony detail of the ulnar-sided metacarpals.
Bones: No displaced fracture is seen through the splint.
Alignment: Unchanged from the earlier study. No dislocation.
Joints: Joint spaces are preserved.
impression: No displaced fracture is seen through the splint. Alignment is unchanged.

clinical.reason: Right hand injury; ulnar gutter splint applied. Post-splint radiographs.

report.title: LUNG, DIGITAL SLIDE, H&E
report.specimen: Lung tissue: one H&E-stained slide, received as a whole-slide image.
microscopic: Sections show lung parenchyma involved by an infiltrating adenocarcinoma, forming irregular glands and small solid nests in a desmoplastic stroma. The adjacent alveolar parenchyma is preserved.
